title: I Let the Homebrew Kegerator Tap Hours Catch the Club Prez Who Camped My Coupler

parts.text: I opened kegerator two at 6:09 p.m. and prez Laird was already pouring through my numbered coupler. The magnet said: ONE TAP. NINETY MINUTES. COUPLER STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-three, club member, holding a gravity sheet that listed our beer. Laird shrugged. "Prez is the tap." I photographed the magnet, the booking, and his pint on my drip tray. Then I asked for the tap log. At 6:17 the cellar pinged why Laird's name was on my coupler. I kept my voice cellar-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A magnet is only a magnet until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The cellar can see Laird's pint on my drip tray during our booking.

social.video_title: He poured through my numbered coupler on my tap — Part 1/2
social.description: Kegerator, a prez on my drip tray, a ninety-minute clock he posted. I logged the pour. Would you have asked for the tap log?

parts.text: Laird called it a sample until the cellar asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the magnet, and the pint still. The coupler went back to my keg. Laird ran his own ninety and told the next prez atmosphere was always about foam. Foam is a word prez uses when a booking exists. Tap policy now has a second line: PREZ IS NOT THE TAP. I keep our coupler on a labeled hook. Laird brown-bags his jokes. The kegerator finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Tap log, numbered coupler, and a second line on the magnet. Was a sample ever my drip tray?
